components: a left vertical that flicks up to the right at its foot
a short upper stroke on the right
a longer lower stroke that curves down on the left and runs out to the right
strokeOrder: draw the left vertical from top to bottom, then without lifting turn and flick up to the right
lift, draw the short upper stroke from left to right
lift, begin at the left and curve down, then run out to the right along the base
strokeOrderNote: KanjiVG's 0306b file records に as three stroke paths in this order and direction: the left vertical with its flick, the upper stroke, then the lower curve; so there are two pen lifts.

strokeOrderSource.citation: KanjiVG, kanji/0306b.svg, hiragana に (U+306B HIRAGANA LETTER NI), three stroke paths kvg:0306b-s1 to s3 (Ulrich Apel and contributors, CC BY-SA 3.0)
strokeOrderSource.variation: KanjiVG stores each stroke as one directed path in writing order: s1 is the left vertical drawn top to bottom, which turns at its foot and flicks up to the right without lifting; s2 is the upper stroke drawn left to right, ending in a small turn down and back to the left that the print glyph does not show; s3 starts at the left, curves down and runs out to the right along the base, rising slightly at its end. Only the order and direction are taken from that file. The learner path's coordinates are the bundled Noto Sans JP outline's own medial line, so the print glyph's proportions, not KanjiVG's handwriting-style ones, decide where each stroke runs. Where the print glyph's left vertical runs on below the point the flick leaves it, the path goes down to the foot of that ink and climbs back a short way before the flick.

notes: Third sign of こんにちは.
